zh: 10年间有多位从各地来的弟兄姊妹来看望在伯大尼服事的弟兄姊妹，每次与他们相调都使我们得着丰富供应。尤其是美国南加州的张弟兄与台湾的王姊妹留给我们许多深刻的印象。弟兄姊妹无论是在属灵还是物质方面都向我们涌流了丰富的爱。我们一直在这身体交通的水流里，这流一直在增长，并且越过越丰富。
en: Over the past ten years, many brothers and sisters from various places came to visit the serving brothers and sisters in Bethany, and every time we blended with them, we received a rich supply. In particular, Brother Chang from Southern California, USA, and Sister Wang from Taiwan left us with many deep impressions. Whether in spiritual or material aspects, the brothers and sisters poured out a rich love toward us. We have always been in this flow of the fellowship of the Body, and this flow has been continually growing and becoming richer and richer.
norm_zh: 10年间有多位从各地来的弟兄姊妹来看望在伯大尼服事的弟兄姊妹每次与他们相调都使我们得着丰富供应尤其是美国南加州的张弟兄与台湾的王姊妹留给我们许多深刻的印象弟兄姊妹无论是在属灵还是物质方面都向我们涌流了丰富的爱我们一直在这身体交通的水流里这流一直在增长并且越过越丰富
norm_en: Over the past ten years many brothers and sisters from various places came to visit the serving brothers and sisters in Bethany and every time we blended with them we received a rich supply In particular Brother Chang from Southern California USA and Sister Wang from Taiwan left us with many deep impressions Whether in spiritual or material aspects the brothers and sisters poured out a rich love toward us We have always been in this flow of the fellowship of the Body and this flow has been continually growing and becoming richer and richer

zh: 很多弟兄姊妹虽不便与我们见面，但在祷告中常常不住地提到我们，实在给我们莫大的扶持与供应。有一次回老家，老家的父老跟我们讲到，每周全召会都会为你们守望祷告。听到后里面就很被加强，也深知我们的服事离不开弟兄姊妹的守望。
en: Although it was not convenient for many brothers and sisters to meet with us, they continually mentioned us in their prayers, which truly gave us great support and supply. Once when we went back to our hometown, the older ones in our hometown told us that the entire church kept a watch in prayer for us every week. Upon hearing this, our inner man was greatly strengthened, and we deeply knew that our service cannot do without the watching of the brothers and sisters.
norm_zh: 很多弟兄姊妹虽不便与我们见面但在祷告中常常不住地提到我们实在给我们莫大的扶持与供应有一次回老家老家的父老跟我们讲到每周全召会都会为你们守望祷告听到后里面就很被加强也深知我们的服事离不开弟兄姊妹的守望
norm_en: Although it was not convenient for many brothers and sisters to meet with us they continually mentioned us in their prayers which truly gave us great support and supply Once when we went back to our hometown the older ones in our hometown told us that the entire church kept a watch in prayer for us every week Upon hearing this our inner man was greatly strengthened and we deeply knew that our service cannot do without the watching of the brothers and sisters

zh: 2024年主预备我们有机会赴台湾参加国际华语特会，弟兄们听说伯大尼的弟兄姊妹要去，刚好他们也有安排特别的行程，就邀请我们一起，带我们与台湾的多地的召会多有交通，我们不但在特会中见证了一个新人的一，也实际地经历了基督身体的实际，在这独一的职事里，我们用同样的口，说同样的话。
en: In 2024, the Lord prepared an opportunity for us to go to Taiwan to attend the International Chinese-speaking Conference. When the brothers heard that the brothers and sisters from Bethany were going, and since they also happened to have scheduled a special itinerary, they invited us to join them, leading us to have much fellowship with the churches in many localities in Taiwan. Not only did we witness the oneness of the one new man in the conference, but we also practically experienced the reality of the Body of Christ. In this unique ministry, we speak the same thing with one mouth.

zh: 2、积极融入当地召会生活，积极配搭召会各样行动
en: 2. Actively Integrating into the Local Church Life, and Actively Coordinating in All the Moves of the Church

norm_en: 2 Actively Integrating into the Local Church Life and Actively Coordinating in All the Moves of the Church

zh: 召会生活也是我们活力来源之一，每周我们有两次的外出福音，有小排聚会、祷告聚会、主日聚会、事奉交通，也会根据圣徒的时间去家聚会，暹粒也常有海外的开展团来开展，每次开展团来我们都会将空闲的时间尽量摆上。借着福音、牧养我们也很被加强。每次外出福音、牧养也使我们喜乐。
en: The church life is also one of the sources of our vitality. Every week we go out for the gospel twice, and we have small group meetings, prayer meetings, Lord's Day meetings, and service fellowship; we also go to home meetings according to the saints' schedules. In Siem Reap, there are also frequently overseas propagation teams coming to propagate, and every time a propagation team comes, we do our best to offer up our spare time. Through the gospel and shepherding, we are also greatly strengthened. Every time we go out for the gospel and shepherding, we are made joyful.
norm_zh: 召会生活也是我们活力来源之一每周我们有两次的外出福音有小排聚会祷告聚会主日聚会事奉交通也会根据圣徒的时间去家聚会暹粒也常有海外的开展团来开展每次开展团来我们都会将空闲的时间尽量摆上借着福音牧养我们也很被加强每次外出福音牧养也使我们喜乐

zh: 我们也为当地召会做了一些牧养材料，有文字、视频诗歌等，我们自己做的资料也常常被用作小排聚会与家聚会，每次用到自己做的材料里面都会更加宝贝文字工作，也更加肯定文字服事工作的价值。如李弟兄在一九八四年《忠信殷勤的传扬真理—关于文字服事》一书中的第五章中讲到：
en: We have also made some shepherding materials for the local church, including literature, video hymns, and so forth. The materials we made themselves are also frequently used for small group meetings and home meetings. Every time we use the materials we made, we treasure the publication work even more within us and affirm even more the value of the publication service. As Brother Lee spoke in chapter 5 of the 1984 book, *Faithfully and Diligently Propagating the Truth—Concerning the Publication Service*:

zh: “文字工作非常有价值，我信主会认这个账。你们要祷告，求主给你们几个人。主若将人赐给你们，你们要宝贝，慢慢地多方成全。譬如倪弟兄三十年的职事里，在文字工作上，没有几个人能帮助他。有些人虽然文笔不错，写写家讯还可以，但真要编辑文字，才知道不是那么简单。所以一定要求主怜悯，赐给你们几个人，能像你们一样，有心志、有异象、有眼光，看见文字工作的效益广而久，感力深刻，完全值得全心全力去作。”（李常受文集一九八四年第五册，忠信殷勤的传扬真理—关于文字服事，第五章　关于文字服事的交通）
en: "The publication work is very valuable, and I believe that the Lord will acknowledge this. We must pray and ask the Lord to give us some to join us in this labor. If the Lord gives us some people, then we must treasure them and gradually perfect them in every way. For example, in Brother Nee's thirty years of ministry, there were not very many who could help him in the publication work. Even though some people could write well, they could contribute only some news articles about the local churches. When they were asked to actually edit the publications, they realized that it was not a simple task. Therefore, we must ask the Lord to have mercy and to give us people like-souled, who would have the will, vision, and view to see that it is absolutely worth laboring on the publications with our whole heart and our whole strength because the effect of this work is long lasting and widespread, and it touches people deeply."

zh: 我们的服事也常与台湾福音书房有交通，积极配合台湾福音书房做一些研发，做出适合推广的材料，或者根据书房的需要来做资料。
en: Our service also frequently has fellowship with the Taiwan Gospel Book Room, actively cooperating with the Taiwan Gospel Book Room to do some research and development, making materials suitable for propagation, or making materials according to the needs of the Book Room.

zh: 伯大尼十年间对主恢复中的职事宝库做了大量的整理，也做出了大量的资料。但我们从未对任何人开放，主要目的是做出一个完整齐备的资料库，如果书房有哪一面的需要就推荐给他们，如果暂时未用到，就先保存起来。
en: Over the past ten years, Bethany has done a great deal of sorting out of the storehouse of the ministry in the Lord's recovery, and has also produced a large amount of materials. However, we have never opened this to any person, our main purpose being to build a complete and comprehensive database, so that if the Book Room has a need in any aspect, we can recommend it to them; if it is not used for the time being, we will keep it preserved first.
norm_zh: 伯大尼十年间对主恢复中的职事宝库做了大量的整理也做出了大量的资料但我们从未对任何人开放主要目的是做出一个完整齐备的资料库如果书房有哪一面的需要就推荐给他们如果暂时未用到就先保存起来

zh: 我们盼望能够更多的与书房有交通，在文字服事方面彼此切磋，能够研究出更高品质的材料，更有效的推广方式，让“神的话……日见扩长，越发繁增”（徒十二24）。

zh: 1	神；圣经中，头一个对神的称呼，自然是“神”；在旧约希伯来文里面，“神”字至少有“伊罗欣”，“伊勒”，“伊罗亚”三个不同的字，各字含意不同—创一1、26，十四18~20，申三二15：
en: 1. God; in the Bible, the first name by which God is called is God; in the Old Testament, there are at least three different Hebrew words for God—Elohim, El, and Eloah, each with a distinct meaning—Gen. 1:1, 26; 14:18-20; Deut. 32:15:
norm_zh: 1神圣经中头一个对神的称呼自然是神在旧约希伯来文里面神字至少有伊罗欣伊勒伊罗亚三个不同的字各字含意不同创一126十四1820申三二15
norm_en: 1 God in the Bible the first name by which God is called is God in the Old Testament there are at least three different Hebrew words for GodElohim El and Eloah each with a distinct meaningGen 11 26 141820 Deut 3215

zh: a	伊罗欣（Elohim）；伊罗欣在原文是由两个字合成的；头一个字意为强有力者，第二个字意为起誓约束自己；起誓说出神的信实，强有力说出神的大能；神是一位信实的大能者；旧约圣经用伊罗欣这个名字，共有两千五百多次—创一1。
en: a. Elohim; in Hebrew, Elohim is composed of two parts; the first part El means one who is strong and powerful, and the second part ohim means to bind oneself with an oath; oath-making reveals God's faithfulness; being strong and powerful reveals God's might; God is a faithful mighty One; the name Elohim is used more than two thousand five hundred times in the Old Testament—Gen. 1:1.
norm_zh: a伊罗欣Elohim伊罗欣在原文是由两个字合成的头一个字意为强有力者第二个字意为起誓约束自己起誓说出神的信实强有力说出神的大能神是一位信实的大能者旧约圣经用伊罗欣这个名字共有两千五百多次创一1
norm_en: a Elohim in Hebrew Elohim is composed of two parts the first part El means one who is strong and powerful and the second part ohim means to bind oneself with an oath oathmaking reveals Gods faithfulness being strong and powerful reveals Gods might God is a faithful mighty One the name Elohim is used more than two thousand five hundred times in the Old TestamentGen 11

zh: b	伊勒（El）；伊勒是个单数字，意思是“为首的大能者”；“居首位的大能者”；本字在旧约中共用了二百五十次，第一次用在创世记十四章十八、十九、二十、二十二节，表明神是在天地间居首位，尊高的大能者。
en: b. El; El is a word in singular form, meaning "the first mighty One, the preeminent mighty One"; this word is used approximately two hundred and fifty times in the Old Testament; it is first used in Genesis 14:18-20 and 22, revealing that God is the preeminent, high, and mighty One in the universe.
norm_zh: b伊勒El伊勒是个单数字意思是为首的大能者居首位的大能者本字在旧约中共用了二百五十次第一次用在创世记十四章十八十九二十二十二节表明神是在天地间居首位尊高的大能者
norm_en: b El El is a word in singular form meaning the first mighty One the preeminent mighty One this word is used approximately two hundred and fifty times in the Old Testament it is first used in Genesis 141820 and 22 revealing that God is the preeminent high and mighty One in the universe

zh: c	伊罗亚（Eloah）；伊罗亚是伊罗欣的单数字，是从阿拉Alah这个字生出来的；阿拉是敬拜的意思，所以伊罗亚的意思是说，神是“当受敬拜的大能者”；本字在旧约中共用了五十六次，头一次用在申命记三十二章十五、十七节。
en: c. Eloah; Eloah is the singular form of Elohim, derived from the word Alah; Alah means "to worship"; therefore, Eloah denotes that God is the mighty One to be worshipped; this word is used fifty-six times in the Old Testament; it is first used in Deuteronomy 32:15 and 17.
norm_zh: c伊罗亚Eloah伊罗亚是伊罗欣的单数字是从阿拉Alah这个字生出来的阿拉是敬拜的意思所以伊罗亚的意思是说神是当受敬拜的大能者本字在旧约中共用了五十六次头一次用在申命记三十二章十五十七节
norm_en: c Eloah Eloah is the singular form of Elohim derived from the word Alah Alah means to worship therefore Eloah denotes that God is the mighty One to be worshipped this word is used fiftysix times in the Old Testament it is first used in Deuteronomy 3215 and 17

zh: 2	耶和华（Jehovah）；在旧约里，最常见的神的名字，就是耶和华；这个字在希伯来文里头，是三个字合成的；“耶”指“现在是”，“和”指“从前是”，“华”指“永远是”；所以耶和华这个字翻成中文，就是“昔是，今是，永远长是”—出三14~15：
en: 2. Jehovah; the name of God that occurs most frequently in the Old Testament is Jehovah; in Hebrew this name is composed of three words: Je means "is," ho means "was," and vah means "will be"; therefore, Jehovah translated into English is "the One who is, was, and always will be"—Exo. 3:14-15:

zh: a	在新约中，主耶稣也常称自己为“我是”，这可以看约翰八章二十四、二十八、五十八，这三节圣经；新约中的“我是”，就是旧约里的“耶和华”，耶和华就是说，神是一切。

zh: 1	赛阿司（Theos）；赛阿司就是神，等于旧约的伊勒，伊罗亚，伊罗欣；这字在旧约里常是指着三而一的神说的；在新约里就有时用来称呼父神，有时用来称呼子神，还有时用来称呼灵神—彼前一3，来一8，徒五3~4。
en: 1. Theos; Theos means "God"; it is equivalent to El, Eloah, and Elohim in the Old Testament. zh: （二）到了创世记一章二十六至二十七节，这一位伊罗欣的神，称自己为“我们”，这又是个多数的称呼。并且在创世记三章二十二节，当亚当吃了善恶树的果子，神说，那人已经和“我们”相似了。创世记十一章七节，当世人建造巴别塔时，神又说，“我们”要下去，在那里变乱他们的口音。以赛亚六章八节，神又说，我可以差遣谁呢？谁肯为“我们”去呢？还有约翰十七章十一、二十二节，主耶稣也说，要门徒合而为一，像“我们”合一一样。神一再的自称为“我们”。
en: 2) In Genesis 1:26-27, God who is Elohim refers to Himself as "Us," another plural term. Also in Genesis 3:22, when Adam ate of the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, God said, "The man has become like one of Us." In Genesis 11:7, when the children of men were building the tower of Babel, God again said, "Let Us go down and there confound their language." Still again in Isaiah 6:8, God says, "Whom shall I send? Who will go for Us?" Furthermore, in John 17:11 and 22 the Lord Jesus also said that the disciples might be one "even as We are." God repeatedly refers to Himself as "Us" and "We."

zh: 伊罗亚是伊罗欣的单数字，是从阿拉Alah这个字生出来的。阿拉是敬拜的意思，所以伊罗亚的意思是说，神是“当受敬拜的大能者”。本字在旧约中共用了五十六次，头一次用在申命记三十二章十五、十七节。
en: Eloah is the singular form of Elohim, derived from the word Alah. Alah means "to worship"; therefore, Eloah denotes that God is "the mighty One to be worshipped." This word is used fifty-six times in the Old Testament; it is first used in Deuteronomy 32:15 and 17.

zh: 在旧约里，最常见的神的名字，就是耶和华。这个字在希伯来文里头，是三个字合成的，刚好“耶”代表一个字，“和”代表一个字，“华”又代表一个字。“耶”指“现在是”，“和”指“从前是”，“华”指“永远是”。所以耶和华这个字翻成中文，就是“昔是，今是，永远长是”。“是”也可以翻成“在”，启示录一章八节就翻成“昔在，今在，永远长在”。所以耶和华的意思是说，神是“昔在，今在，永远长在”的；也是“昔是，今是，永远长是”的。此外这字也有“自有永有”，“无始无终”；“永存不没”；和“永是不变”的意思。出埃及记三章十四，十五两节里的“我是自有永有的”，就是耶和华的意思。
en: The name of God that occurs most frequently in the Old Testament is Jehovah. In Hebrew this name is composed of three words: Je represents a word, ho represents a word, and vah also represents a word. Je means "is," ho means "was," and vah means "will be." Therefore, Jehovah translated into English is "the One who is, was, and always will be." The verb to be can also be translated as "to be present"; thus, Revelation 1:8 translates it as "He who is present, who was present, and who will be present forever." So Jehovah means that God is present, was present, and will be present forever, and also that He is, was, and will be forever. In addition, this word also means "self-existing and ever-existing, without beginning or end, forever remaining and never ceasing to be," and "forever unchanging." In Exodus 3:14-15, "I AM WHO I AM" is the meaning of Jehovah.

zh: 巴特尔翻作中文是“父”。这是神在新约里特别将祂自己启示出来的名字。神是父，是说到神是一切的源头，一切的根源，一切的起头，一切的开始。父就是源头、开始的意思。约翰二十章十七节，主耶稣复活之后，对门徒们说，“我要升上去见我的父，也是你们的父。”约壹三章一节说，“你看父赐给我们是何等的慈爱，使我们得称为神的儿女，”那里的父都是巴特尔。
en: Pater, translated into English is "Father." By the name Father in the New Testament, God reveals Himself to us in a particular way. God as the Father denotes God as the source of all things, the origin of all things, the initiation of all things, and the beginning of all things. The name Father implies the source, the beginning. In John 20:17, after His resurrection the Lord said to the disciples, "I ascend to My Father and your Father." First John 3:1 says, "Behold what manner of love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God." The word for Father in these verses is pater.

zh: 在以弗所一章九节、十一节，三章十一节，这三处圣经里头，中文翻译都把“计划”翻作“旨意”。实在希腊原文的意思，不光是旨意，更是照着旨意有了一个计划。计划包括旨意。比方我们可能有意要造一个大会所，但是还没有计划；若是我们已经有了计划，那在计划里面一定是包括定意。
en: In these three passages of Scripture—Ephesians 1:9, 11, and 3:11—the Chinese translation translates "plan" as "will." Actually, the meaning in the Greek original is not only a will but even more, a plan according to the will. A plan includes a will. For example, we may have the intention to build a large meeting hall, but we do not yet have a plan; if we already have a plan, that plan must include our determination.

zh: 从创世记一章二节起，直到创世记二章末了，都是说到复造的事。当时原始的创造淹没在洪水之下，空虚混沌，渊面黑暗，神就来重新造作。祂先吩咐天上的光体发出光来，再吩咐地上的水聚在一起，使地露出。所以复造就是把经过审判的天地，重新整理恢复一下。复造是以宇宙为范围，以万有作凭借，以人类作中心。
en: The matter of restoration is spoken of from Genesis 1:2 to the end of Genesis 2. The original creation was submerged under water; it was waste and emptiness, with darkness on the surface of the deep. Therefore, God came in to restore. First, He ordered the heavenly luminaries to give light, and then He ordered the water on the earth to gather together so that dry land would appear. zh: 挪亚一家要借着方舟得救，必须进到方舟里面。我们要靠着基督得救，也必须进到基督里面。所以在新约里，每一次题到信主耶稣的时候，原文的“信”字后面，都有“到里面去”的字根。信到主耶稣里面，意思就是和主耶稣联合。没有联合，就没有代替。挪亚一家八口藏在方舟里面，洪水所击打的是方舟，而不是他们。神所看见的也是方舟，而不是他们。方舟所以成了他们的代替，乃是根据他们和方舟的联合。同样，牺牲所以能代替亚当受神击杀，也是因为亚当穿到牺牲里面，和牺牲联合为一。不仅如此，当以色列人过逾越节的时侯，他们也要躲在抹血的屋子里，并且要把羊羔的肉吃到里面，这些都是联合的故事。妓女喇合一家的得救，也是因为他们全家人聚集在系着红绳的屋子里面。以后以色列人进了迦南，设立了六座逃城，误犯罪的必须跑到逃城里面，才能免去刑罚。神在这里很清楚的把救法启示出来，有联合才有代替。主耶稣所以能代替我们，是因为我们和祂有了联结。所以林后五章二十一节说，“神使那无罪的替我们成为罪；好叫我们在祂里面成为神的义。”我们必须在祂里面，才能成为神的义。
en: In order for Noah and his family to be saved through the ark, they had to enter into the ark. For us to be saved through Christ, we must enter into Christ. Therefore, whenever the matter of believing in Jesus is spoken of in the New Testament, the Greek word for to believe is always followed by the preposition into. To believe into the Lord Jesus means to be identified with the Lord Jesus; without identification there is no substitution. Noah's family of eight was hidden within the ark; the floodwater assailed the ark instead of them. God saw the ark instead of them. The ark became their substitute by virtue of their being identified with the ark. In the same way, a sacrifice could be slaughtered in place of Adam because Adam was identified with the sacrifice. Furthermore, when the Israelites observed the passover, they hid within houses that were sprinkled with blood and consumed the meat of the lamb. These are all stories of identification. Rahab the harlot and her family were saved because they gathered in a house with a scarlet thread tied to it. Later, the Israelites entered Canaan and established six cities of refuge. Those who unintentionally committed sin had to flee into a city of refuge to avoid punishment. Here God clearly reveals the way of salvation—there must be identification in order for there to be substitution. The Lord Jesus can replace us because we have been identified with Him. Therefore, 2 Corinthians 5:21 says, "Him who did not know sin He made sin on our behalf that we might become the righteousness of God in Him." We must be in Him to become the righteousness of God.

zh: 教会应该都是蒙救赎的，但是也有不蒙救赎的成分被带进来，比如肉体、人意、世界、罪恶、魔鬼的事、败坏的事，这些都是神所要审判的。在启示录二、三章的七封书信里面告诉我们，历代所有的教会，里面都有不蒙救赎的成分，所以启示录一开头，那位救赎的主就来作了审判的主，审判祂所救赎的教会。当祂显出来的时候，眼目像火焰，口里出来一把两刃的利剑，脚像光明的铜，这些都是审判的光景。
en: The churches should be fully redeemed; yet there are some unredeemable elements that have been brought into the churches. For example, the flesh, the will of man, the world, sin, the things of the devil, and corrupted things are being judged by God. The seven epistles in Revelation chapters 2 and 3 tell us that all the churches throughout the generations have had some unredeemable elements. Therefore, at the very beginning of Revelation the redeeming Lord comes as the judging Lord to judge all of His redeemed churches. When He is manifested, His eyes are like a flame of fire, a sharp two-edged sword proceeds out of His mouth, and His feet are like shining bronze; this is a scene of judgment.

zh: 1	神；圣经中，头一个对神的称呼，自然是“神”；在旧约希伯来文里面，“神”字至少有“伊罗欣”，“伊勒”，“伊罗亚”三个不同的字，各字含意不同—创一1、26，十四18~20，申三二15：（李常受文集一九五九年第三册，圣经的十条路线，第一篇）
en: 1. God; in the Bible, the first name by which God is called is God; in the Old Testament, there are at least three different Hebrew words for God—Elohim, El, and Eloah, each with a distinct meaning.—Gen. 1:1, 26; 14:18-20; Deut. 32:15:

zh: a	伊罗欣（Elohim）；伊罗欣在原文是由两个字合成的；头一个字意为强有力者，第二个字意为起誓约束自己；起誓说出神的信实，强有力说出神的大能；神是一位信实的大能者；旧约圣经用伊罗欣这个名字，共有两千五百多次—创一1。（李常受文集一九五九年第三册，圣经的十条路线，第一篇）
en: a. Elohim; in Hebrew, Elohim is composed of two parts; the first part El means one who is strong and powerful, and the second part ohim means to bind oneself with an oath; oath-making reveals God's faithfulness; being strong and powerful reveals God's might; God is a faithful mighty One; this name is used more than two thousand five hundred times in the Old Testament.—Gen. 1:1.
norm_zh: a伊罗欣Elohim伊罗欣在原文是由两个字合成的头一个字意为强有力者第二个字意为起誓约束自己起誓说出神的信实强有力说出神的大能神是一位信实的大能者旧约圣经用伊罗欣这个名字共有两千五百多次创一1李常受文集一九五九年第三册圣经的十条路线第一篇
norm_en: a Elohim in Hebrew Elohim is composed of two parts the first part El means one who is strong and powerful and the second part ohim means to bind oneself with an oath oathmaking reveals Gods faithfulness being strong and powerful reveals Gods might God is a faithful mighty One this name is used more than two thousand five hundred times in the Old TestamentGen 11

zh: b	伊勒（El）；伊勒是个单数字，意思是“为首的大能者”；“居首位的大能者”；本字在旧约中共用了二百五十次，第一次用在创世记十四章十八、十九、二十、二十二节，表明神是在天地间居首位，尊高的大能者。（李常受文集一九五九年第三册，圣经的十条路线，第一篇）
en: b. El; El is a word in singular form, meaning "the first mighty One, the preeminent mighty One"; this word is used approximately two hundred and fifty times in the Old Testament; it is first used in Genesis 14:18-20 and 22, revealing that God is the preeminent, high, and mighty One in the universe.
norm_zh: b伊勒El伊勒是个单数字意思是为首的大能者居首位的大能者本字在旧约中共用了二百五十次第一次用在创世记十四章十八十九二十二十二节表明神是在天地间居首位尊高的大能者李常受文集一九五九年第三册圣经的十条路线第一篇
norm_en: b El El is a word in singular form meaning the first mighty One the preeminent mighty One this word is used approximately two hundred and fifty times in the Old Testament it is first used in Genesis 141820 and 22 revealing that God is the preeminent high and mighty One in the universe

zh: c	伊罗亚（Eloah）；伊罗亚是伊罗欣的单数字，是从阿拉Alah这个字生出来的；阿拉是敬拜的意思，所以伊罗亚的意思是说，神是“当受敬拜的大能者”；本字在旧约中共用了五十六次，头一次用在申命记三十二章十五、十七节。（李常受文集一九五九年第三册，圣经的十条路线，第一篇）
en: c. Eloah; Eloah is the singular form of Elohim, derived from the word Alah; Alah means "to worship"; therefore, Eloah denotes that God is "the mighty One to be worshipped"; this word is used fifty-six times in the Old Testament; it is first used in Deuteronomy 32:15 and 17.
norm_zh: c伊罗亚Eloah伊罗亚是伊罗欣的单数字是从阿拉Alah这个字生出来的阿拉是敬拜的意思所以伊罗亚的意思是说神是当受敬拜的大能者本字在旧约中共用了五十六次头一次用在申命记三十二章十五十七节李常受文集一九五九年第三册圣经的十条路线第一篇

zh: 2	耶和华（Jehovah）；在旧约里，最常见的神的名字，就是耶和华；这个字在希伯来文里头，是三个字合成的；“耶”指“现在是”，“和”指“从前是”，“华”指“永远是”；所以耶和华这个字翻成中文，就是“昔是，今是，永远长是”—出三14~15：（李常受文集一九五九年第三册，圣经的十条路线，第一篇）
en: 2. Jehovah; the name of God that occurs most frequently in the Old Testament is Jehovah; in Hebrew this name is composed of three words; Je means "is," ho means "was," and vah means "will be"; therefore, Jehovah translated into English is "the One who is, was, and always will be".—Exo. 3:14-15:

zh: a	在新约中，主耶稣也常称自己为“我是”，这可以看约翰八章二十四、二十八、五十八，这三节圣经；新约中的“我是”，就是旧约里的“耶和华”，耶和华就是说，神是一切。（李常受文集一九五九年第三册，圣经的十条路线，第一篇）
en: a. In the New Testament, the Lord Jesus referred to Himself often as I Am. This can be seen in John 8:24, 28, and 58; I Am in the New Testament is Jehovah in the Old Testament; this name means that God is everything.

zh: b	亚（Jah）；这字是耶和华的简称，第一次用在出埃及记十五章二节；在诗篇中多与“阿利路”联起来用，就是我们所常见的“阿利路亚”，意即“要赞美耶和华”；在以赛亚书中也用这名字；在这三卷书中，亚字大约用了四十九次。（李常受文集一九五九年第三册，圣经的十条路线，第一篇）
en: b. Jah; this word is an abbreviated form of Jehovah; it is first used in Exodus 15:2; in the book of Psalms, it is combined with hallelu to form the frequently used word hallelujah, meaning "praise Jehovah"; this name is also used in Isaiah; it is used forty-nine times in these three books.

zh: 1	赛阿司（Theos）；赛阿司就是神，等于旧约的伊勒，伊罗亚，伊罗欣；这字在旧约里常是指着三而一的神说的；在新约里就有时用来称呼父神，有时用来称呼子神，还有时用来称呼灵神—彼前一3，来一8，徒五3~4。（李常受文集一九五九年第三册，圣经的十条路线，第一篇）
en: 1. Theos; Theos means "God"; it is equivalent to El, Eloah, and Elohim in the Old Testament; in the Old Testament, God usually refers to the Triune God; in the New Testament, God sometimes refers to God the Father, sometimes to God the Son, and sometimes to God the Spirit—1 Pet. 1:3; Heb. 1:8; Acts 5:3-4.

zh: 2	巴特尔（Bater）；巴特尔翻作中文是“父”；这是神在新约里特别将祂自己启示出来的名字；神是父，是说到神是一切的源头，一切的根源，一切的起头，一切的开始；父就是源头、开始的意思—约二十17，约壹三1。（李常受文集一九五九年第三册，圣经的十条路线，第一篇）
en: 2. Pater; Pater, translated into English is "Father"; by the name Father in the New Testament, God reveals Himself to us in a particular way; God as the Father denotes God as the source of all things, the origin of all things, the initiation of all things, and the beginning of all things; the name Father implies the source, the beginning—John 20:17; 1 John 3:1.

zh: 3	代司拍提司（Despotes）；代司拍提司中文翻作“主宰”，简单一点翻作“主”；不过这和旧约的“阿多乃”（Adonai），中文翻作主人的“主”，大有分别；这里指着一位掌权的主说的—路二29，徒四24，启六10。（李常受文集一九五九年第三册，圣经的十条路线，第一篇）
en: 3. Despotes; in English, despotes is translated "Sovereign Master," or simply "Master"; however, this is very different from the Old Testament adonai, which is translated "Lord"; here the word despotes refers to a master with authority—Luke 2:29; Acts 4:24; Rev. 6:10.

en: 4. Kurios; the word Lord in Matthew 1:20 and Mark 12:29 is kurios, referring to the Lord Jesus; when the New Testament quotes an Old Testament verse, kurios is often used in place of Jehovah; kurios is a title of the Lord Jesus in His divinity.

en: 5. Jesus; the Greek word Jesus and the Hebrew word Joshua are the same word; so the meaning of Joshua, or Jesus, is "Jehovah the Savior," or "the salvation of Jehovah"; Jesus in particular refers to the Lord being a man. This is a title of the Lord Jesus in His humanity—Luke 1:31; Matt. 1:21.

zh: 一	计划；在以弗所一章九节、十一节，三章十一节，这三处圣经里头，中文翻译都把“计划”翻作“旨意”；实在希腊原文的意思，不光是旨意，更是照着旨意有了一个计划；计划包括旨意；神的计划，乃是在永远里头的事：（李常受文集一九五九年第三册，圣经的十条路线，第一篇）

zh: 撒但，就是天使长，背叛了神，并且三分之一的天使也同他联合背叛。（赛十四12~15，结二八13~18，启十二4。）天使的数目是无数的，所以三分之一的天使与撒但联合背叛，意思是说，有很大数目的天使跟从了他。撒但背叛之后，神就进来审判。宇宙在神审判之下变成混乱：诸天变成黑暗，地变为荒废虚空。（伯九5~7，创一2上。）因为撒但的背叛不仅玷污了地，也玷污了诸天，所以地和诸天都受了神的审判。诸天变成黑暗，地变为荒废虚空。那就是混乱。创世记一章一节说，“起初神创造天地”。在这里我们看见，神在创造宇宙中的经纶。按照正确的翻译，二节上半接着说，“而地变为荒废虚空”。这指明地变得混沌、混乱。
en: Satan, the archangel, rebelled against God, and one third of the angels joined him in his rebellion (Isa. 14:12-15; Ezek. 28:13-18; Rev. 12:4). The number of the angels is countless, so one third of the angels joining with Satan in his rebellion means that a great number of angels followed him. After Satan's rebellion, God came in to judge. Under God's judgment the universe became a chaos: the heavens became dark, and the earth became waste and void (Job 9:5-7; Gen. 1:2a). Because Satan's rebellion defiled not only the earth but also the heavens, both the earth and the heavens were judged by God. The heavens became dark, and the earth became waste and void. That was chaos. Genesis 1:1 says, "In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth." Here we see God's economy in the creation of the universe. According to the correct translation, the first half of verse 2 continues, saying, "But the earth became waste and void." This indicates that the earth became a chaos, a confusion.

zh: 在旧造里撒但的混乱，开始于撒但这蛇试诱人吃善恶知识树。（创三1~5。）善和恶都是属于同一棵树，如今我们在同一个人身上，可以看见善，也可以看见恶。创世记三章六节和七节给我们看见，人受了骗而堕落了。这是在恢复之宇宙中的混乱。这结果的第二面，乃是通往生命树的路向堕落的人关闭。这条路要一直关闭，直到基督来完成救赎，重新打开通往生命树的路。
en: The satanic chaos in the old creation began with Satan as the serpent tempting man to take of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil (Gen. 3:1-5). Both good and evil belong to the same tree, and now with the same person we can see good and also evil. Genesis 3:6 and 7 show us that man was deceived and became fallen. This was the chaos in the restored universe. The second aspect of this result was that the way to the tree of life was closed to fallen man. This way was closed until Christ came to accomplish redemption to reopen the way to the tree of life.

zh: 亚当可能有许多儿子，但圣经只用亚伯和该隐作为模型。亚伯是神圣经纶的模型，该隐是撒但混乱的模型。该隐拒绝神的应许，杀了他的兄弟亚伯，带进神的审判和咒诅。（创四3~16。）他没有献上羊群中的东西（预表基督），而献上他自己劳苦的成果，那得罪了神。一个罪人自己所劳苦的，是没有什么可以献给公义的神，而蒙神悦纳的。该隐献上他自己劳苦的成果给神，似乎是作了好事。但在他所献的被神拒绝后不久，该隐作了一件恶事—杀了他的兄弟。在他身上有善也有恶，指明他必定是属于善恶知识树的。今天在人群社会中，光景也是一样。一面，一个绅士可能作许多善事，另一面，同一个人也作许多恶事。
en: Adam may have had many sons, but the Bible uses only Abel and Cain as models. Abel was a model of the divine economy, and Cain was a model of the satanic chaos. Cain rejected God's promise and killed his brother Abel, bringing in God's judgment and curse (Gen. 4:3-16). He did not offer something from the flock (typifying Christ) but offered the fruit of his own labor, which offended God. There is nothing of a sinner's own labor that can be offered to the righteous God to be accepted by Him. Cain offered the fruit of his own labor to God, which seemed to be a good thing. But shortly after his offering was rejected by God, Cain did an evil thing—he killed his brother. In him there was both good and evil, indicating that he surely belonged to the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. Today in human society the situation is the same. On the one hand, a gentleman may do many good things, but on the other hand, the same person also does many evil things.

zh: 在人更进一步的堕落中，人成了肉体，人的罪极大，以致人受神洪水的审判。（创六3、5~7、13，七10~11、17~23上。）在人终极的堕落里，人在巴别背叛神，高举自己，并敬拜偶像，与撒但联合，以拦阻神圣的经纶。（创十一1~9。）在这时候之前，有一个强人兴起来，名叫宁录。（十8~11。）宁录是敌基督的豫表，他建造了巴别和尼尼微。巴别是偶像之处，在这城的砖块上都写着偶像的名字。在巴别那里，人背叛神，高举自己，并敬拜偶像。
en: In man's further fall, man became flesh, and man's sin was so great that man suffered God's judgment of the flood (Gen. 6:3, 5-7, 13; 7:10-11, 17-23a). In the consummation of man's fall, man rebelled against God, exalted himself, and worshipped the idols at Babel in union with Satan to frustrate the divine economy (Gen. 11:1-9). Before this time, a strong man rose up by the name of Nimrod (Gen. 10:8-11). Nimrod, a type of Antichrist, built Babel and also Nineveh. Babel was a place of idols, and the names of idols were written on the bricks of the city. At Babel man rebelled against God, exalted himself, and worshipped idols.

zh: 以色列人成了有神同在蒙福的客旅，但他们在遵守神诫命的事上，过于自信。（出十九7~8。）神将他们带到西乃山，在那里祂进来与他们相会，并对他们说话。他们过于自信，不认识自己，他们说，“凡耶和华所说的我们都要遵行”。（8上。）这触犯了神，因为这指明他们不认识自己。他们该说，“耶和华啊，你知道我们是堕落的人，我们无法遵行你的话，我们需要你的怜悯、恩典、救赎和拯救”。神喜欢听见这样的话。然而，以色列人所说的完全不同，这得罪了神，祂就颁下了律法。以色列人非常自信，甚至在律法赐给他们之前，就已经干犯了律法。在旷野里，以色列人从神圣经纶的中心线上转到律法的旁线上。（出二十1~21。）
en: The people of Israel had become blessed travelers with God, but they were overconfident in themselves for the keeping of God's commandments (Exo. 19:7-8). God brought them to Mount Sinai, where He came in to meet with them and to speak to them. Being overconfident in themselves and not knowing themselves, they said, "All that the Lord hath spoken we will do" (v. 8a). God was offended by this, for it indicated that they did not know themselves. They should have said, "O Lord, You know that we are a fallen people. We cannot keep Your word. We need Your mercy, grace, redemption, and salvation." God is pleased to hear such a word. However, what the people of Israel spoke was entirely different and was offensive to God, who then proceeded to decree the law. The people, who were so confident in themselves, broke the law even before it was given to them. In the wilderness the people of Israel sidetracked themselves from the central line of the divine economy to the sideline of the law (Exo. 20:1-21).

zh: 大卫落在罪中，他的家变得一团混乱。（撒下十一~十八。）这是大卫犯了谋杀和淫乱之罪的结果。因着大卫的犯罪，结果他的家不再有平安。他的儿子押沙龙，杀了另一个儿子，并背叛了大卫，甚至想要杀害他。所罗门落在罪中，他的国分裂为二。（王上十一1~40。）诸王的衰微，祭司的腐败，申言者的虚假，以色列人的邪恶，都到了无法容忍的地步。这混乱的光景记载在列王纪上、列王纪下、和众申言者的书中。
en: David fell into sin, and his house became a total mess (2 Sam. 11—18). This was the result of David's committing the sins of murder and adultery. Because of David's sinning, his house no longer had peace. His son Absalom killed another son and rebelled against David, even seeking to kill him. Solomon fell into sin, and his kingdom was divided into two (1 Kings 11:1-40). The decline of the kings, the corruption of the priests, the falsehood of the prophets, and the wickedness of the Israelites all reached an intolerable degree. This chaotic situation is recorded in 1 and 2 Kings and in the books of the prophets.

zh: 雅各和耶路撒冷的长老劝保罗守犹太律法的规条。（徒二一18~26。）我们很难相信耶路撒冷的领头长老劝保罗回到圣殿，并且在犹太教的祭司之下，守他们律法的规条。但这正是他们所作的，保罗也顺从了他们的劝导。然而主不容让保罗完成犹太教的仪式。在仪式的最后一天，就起了骚动，保罗被关进监狱。至终，保罗被移转到罗马的监狱。他虽然被释放，但在一年之内，他又再被捕而殉道。你对保罗的情形要怎么说？有些人可能说保罗犯了错，在他的职事上不忠信，那就是为什么他被关进监狱，并且至终被带到罗马直接受该撒的审判。不错，在行传二十一章那里，有极大的混乱。然而，若没有这混乱，我们就不会有以弗所书、腓立比书、歌罗西书、提摩太前后书、和提多书。关于召会生活、基督徒生活、和神的经纶并神圣的分赐这些深奥的真理，都在这些书中。新约若是没有这些书，就是很大的缺欠。当保罗在监狱中的时候，他写了书信，这些书信充满了美妙、高超的启示。这指明混乱至终使一些极超绝的事得以产生。不仅如此，保罗的殉道对历世纪以来的圣徒都是一种激励。因此，仇敌在那混乱的情形中所作的，对神的权益反成了益处。
en: James and the elders in Jerusalem exhorted Paul to keep the ordinances of the Jewish law (Acts 21:18-26). It is hard for us to believe that the leading elders in Jerusalem exhorted Paul to go back to the temple and, under the priests of Judaism, keep the ordinances of their law. But this is exactly what they did, and Paul also followed their advice. However, the Lord did not allow Paul to complete the Judaic ceremony. On the last day of the ceremony, there was turmoil, and Paul was put into prison. Eventually, Paul was transferred to the prison in Rome. Although he was released, within a year he was arrested again and martyred. What would you say about Paul's situation? Some might say that Paul made a mistake and was not faithful in his ministry, and that was the reason he was put into prison and was eventually brought to Rome to be judged directly by Caesar. No doubt, in Acts 21 there was great chaos. However, without this chaos we would not have the books of Ephesians, Philippians, Colossians, 1 and 2 Timothy, and Titus. Deep truths concerning the church life, the Christian life, and God's economy with the divine dispensing are in these books. If these books were not in the New Testament, there would be a great lack. While Paul was in prison, he wrote epistles that are filled with wonderful, high revelation. This indicates that the chaos eventually enabled something most excellent to be produced. Furthermore, Paul's martyrdom has been an encouragement to saints throughout the centuries. Thus, what the enemy did in that chaotic situation became a profit to God's interests.

The divine life, which was concealed in His humanity, needed to be released in order to increase and multiply.

en: Therefore, Christ died not only to take away sin and to destroy Satan but also to release the divine life.

zh: 在祂的复活里，基督成了长子。行传十三章三十三节指明，复活对那人耶稣乃是一次的出生。祂在祂的复活里由神而生，就在许多弟兄中作神的长子。（罗八29。）祂从永远就是神的独生子。（约一18，三16。）在成为肉体以后，借着复活，祂在祂的人性里被神生为神的长子。可以说，在祂的复活里，祂的人性被“子化”了。
en: In His resurrection Christ became the firstborn Son. Acts 13:33 indicates that resurrection was a birth to the man Jesus. He was begotten by God in His resurrection to be the firstborn Son of God among many brothers (Rom. 8:29). He was the only begotten Son of God from eternity (John 1:18; 3:16). After incarnation, through resurrection He was begotten by God in His humanity to be God’s firstborn Son. We may say that in His resurrection His humanity was “sonized.”

zh: 在复活里，基督也成为复合了神性、人性、死与复活的赐生命之灵。（林前十五45下。）这灵乃是三一神的终极完成，也是复活的实际。事实上，这灵就是那是灵的基督（the pneumatic Christ）自己。照着约翰十一章二十五节，复活就是基督自己，而基督现今是赐生命的灵。
en: In resurrection Christ also became the life-giving Spirit (1 Cor. 15:45b), compounded with divinity, humanity, death, and resurrection. This Spirit is the consummation of the Triune God and the reality of resurrection. Actually, this Spirit is the pneumatic Christ Himself. According to John 11:25 resurrection is Christ Himself, and Christ is now the life-giving Spirit.

en: Hence, the life-giving Spirit is the reality of resurrection. When we live in this Spirit, we live in resurrection. When we love others in this Spirit, we love them in resurrection.

zh: 基督被高举，作一切掌权者的元首。（徒五31。）行传五章三十一节说，“这一位，神已将祂高举在自己的右边，作元首，作救主，将悔改和赦罪赐给以色列人。”祂拯救我们的方式是借着作元首。因为祂管制万有，祂就有拯救我们的大能、权柄、能力和性能。在祂的为首之下，我们得救了。祂若愿意，祂甚至有权柄和能力废除君王，为要拯救祂的一个子民。出埃及记对法老和以色列人为奴，神就打发摩西告诉法老，容祂的百姓去。（出五1。）法老拒绝，主就降灾于他，他就请摩西为他恳求主。（出八8、28，九27~28，十16~17。）至终，法老被征服，他释放了以色列人。（出十一1，十二31。）救主借着祂的能力和权柄拯救了祂的子民。（李常受文集一九八九年第四册，使徒的教训与新约中的领导，第二章）
en: Christ was exalted as the Leader over all the rulers (Acts 5:31). Acts 5:31 says, "This One God has exalted to His right hand as a Leader and Savior, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins." The way He saves us is by being the Leader. Because He controls all things, He has the power, authority, ability, and capacity to save us. Under His leadership we have been saved. He has the authority and power, if He should so desire, to remove a king in order to save even one of His people. Concerning Pharaoh and the people of Israel in slavery in Exodus, God sent Moses to tell Pharaoh to let His people go (Exo. 5:1). When Pharaoh refused, the Lord brought the plagues upon him, and he asked Moses to entreat the Lord for him (Exo. 8:8, 28; 9:27-28; 10:16-17). Eventually, Pharaoh was subdued, and he released the people of Israel (Exo. 11:1; 12:31). The Savior saved His people through His power and authority.

zh: 有一天，祂还要再来：“地的四极都要…归向祂；列国的万族，都要…敬拜。…祂在列国中掌权”。（诗二二27∼28。）祂在地上执掌王权，施行公理和公义，（耶二三5，）地上就成了祂的国度；并且祂的国是永远的，祂的权柄存到万代，（诗一四五13，）要永永远远彰显神的荣耀。旧约把基督从已过的永远，到将来的永远，在时间里的经过，都详详细细的预言过了。
en: One day He will come back: "all the ends of the earth / Will ... return to Jehovah, / ... All families of the nations / Will worship" Him, and He will rule among the nations (Psa. 22:27-28). He "will reign as King" and "will execute justice and righteousness" on the earth (Jer. 23:5). Then the earth will become His kingdom; and His kingdom is eternal, and His dominion is throughout all generations (Psa. 145:13) for the expression of God's glory forever and ever. The Old Testament prophesies in detail concerning Christ in eternity past, in His passing through time, and in eternity future.

zh: 所认识、享受、据有、并经历的基督
en: The Christ whom we know, enjoy, possess, and experience
norm_zh: 所认识享受据有并经历的基督
norm_en: The Christ whom we know enjoy possess and experience

zh: 我们所认识、享受、据有、并经历的基督，乃是由那有山、有河、有泉、有平原的宽阔美地所预表。（申八7~10。）照着约书亚记，这不但是犹大支派和便雅悯支派的基督，也是利未支派的基督。在主的恢复里，我们乃是今日的利未人。犹大的分是我们的分，便雅悯的分也是我们的分。这就是说，我们所享受的，是十二支派对基督的一切经历，包括早期的使徒、教父、殉道者、改革者、更正教、奥秘派、摩尔维亚弟兄们、英国弟兄们、内里生命派、福音派和灵恩派。（约书亚记生命读经，第十三篇）
en: The Christ whom we know, enjoy, possess, and experience is typified by the spacious good land of mountains, rivers, brooks, and plains (Deut. 8:7-10). According to the book of Joshua, this is the Christ not only of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin but also of the tribe of Levi. In the Lord’s recovery we are today’s Levites. Judah’s portion is our portion, and Benjamin’s portion also is our portion. This means that we are enjoying all of the experiences of Christ in the twelve tribes, including the early apostles, the church fathers, the martyrs, the reformers, the Protestants, the mystics, the Moravians, the Brethren, the inner life Christians, the evangelicals, and the Pentecostals.

zh: 在圣经开头的地方，就给我们看见精金、珍珠、还有宝石，这些都是建造的材料。到了圣经末了的地方，就给我们看见有一所建筑出来了，是用精金、珍珠和宝石建造成功的。这叫我们知道，神最终所要得着的一个东西，就是一所的建筑，是由祂的儿子来作羔羊，成功救赎之后建造成功的。所以论到基督，不能只看见祂是救赎的，还要看见祂是建造的；祂来救赎，也来建造。神所以创造万有和人类，就是要在宇宙中得着一所的建筑。
en: At the beginning of the Bible we are shown pure gold, pearls, and precious stones, which are all materials for building. At the end of the Bible we see a building that has come forth, built with pure gold, pearls, and precious stones. This lets us know that the ultimate thing God wants to obtain is a building, which is built up after His Son came as the Lamb to accomplish redemption. Therefore, concerning Christ, we must not only see Him as the redeeming One, but we must also see Him as the building One; He came to redeem and also to build. The reason God created all things and mankind is to obtain a building in the universe.

zh: 在全圣经里，一点不差是给我们看见，基督是怎样一回事；但同时也一直给我们看见，基督需要一个教会，如同男子需要一个配偶。圣经一开头就有这样预表的话说，亚当这个人独居不好。到了新约我们就知道，这一个乃是预表基督需要一个配偶。所以在圣经开头的时候，不仅给我们看见一个亚当，还给我们看见怎样从亚当产生一个夏娃来，作了他的配偶，二人成为一体。圣经里有亚当，也有夏娃。使徒保罗说，“这是极大的奥秘，但我是指着基督和教会说的。”你没有办法在圣经里头，只看见基督，而不看见教会。很多人在那里讲以撒，却忽略了利百加。有以撒，也有利百加。在圣经里头，有神在基督里，来和人接触的故事，但在圣经里，人也站在一个非常重要的地位上。圣经里的中心人物，不光有神在基督里，还有人来作神在基督里的配偶。宇宙的夫妇，就是神与人。在宇宙中，神是惟一的男子，人是神的配偶。人若没有神，如同寡妇一样；神若没有人，也如同一个独居的男子一样。在宇宙里头，必须神与人能配合。
en: No doubt the whole Bible shows us Christ. But at the same time it also shows us that Christ needs a church, in the same way that a man needs a wife. From the very beginning the Bible reveals this in a type—that it was not good for Adam to live alone. We know from the New Testament that this typifies the fact that Christ needs a bride. Therefore, at the beginning of the Bible, not only does it reveal to us the one Adam, but it also reveals to us how Eve was produced from Adam to become his bride and how they two became one. There was Adam, and there was Eve. The apostle Paul said, "This mystery is great, but I speak with regard to Christ and the church." In the Bible one cannot just see Christ without seeing the church. Many talk about Isaac and forget about Rebekah. There was Isaac, and there was Rebekah. In the Bible there is the story of God contacting man through Christ, but there is also man occupying a very important position. The central characters in the Bible are not only God in Christ but also man as the bride of God in Christ. The universal couple is God and man. In the universe God is the only male, and man is the counterpart of God. If man is without God, he is like a widow. If God is without man, He is like a bachelor. In the universe there has to be the matching of God with man.
norm_zh: 在全圣经里一点不差是给我们看见基督是怎样一回事但同时也一直给我们看见基督需要一个教会如同男子需要一个配偶圣经一开头就有这样预表的话说亚当这个人独居不好到了新约我们就知道这一个乃是预表基督需要一个配偶所以在圣经开头的时候不仅给我们看见一个亚当还给我们看见怎样从亚当产生一个夏娃来作了他的配偶二人成为一体圣经里有亚当也有夏娃使徒保罗说这是极大的奥秘但我是指着基督和教会说的你没有办法在圣经里头只看见基督而不看见教会很多人在哪里讲以撒却忽略了利百加有以撒也有利百加在圣经里头有神在基督里来和人接触的故事但在圣经里人也站在一个非常重要的地位上圣经里的中心人物不光有神在基督里还有人来作神在基督里的配偶宇宙的夫妇就是神与人在宇宙中神是惟一的男子人是神的配偶人若没有神如同寡妇一样神若没有人也如同一个独居的男子一样在宇宙里头必须神与人能配合
norm_en: No doubt the whole Bible shows us Christ But at the same time it also shows us that Christ needs a church in the same way that a man needs a wife From the very beginning the Bible reveals this in a typethat it was not good for Adam to live alone We know from the New Testament that this typifies the fact that Christ needs a bride Therefore at the beginning of the Bible not only does it reveal to us the one Adam but it also reveals to us how Eve was produced from Adam to become his bride and how they two became one There was Adam and there was Eve The apostle Paul said This mystery is great but I speak with regard to Christ and the church In the Bible one cannot just see Christ without seeing the church Many talk about Isaac and forget about Rebekah There was Isaac and there was Rebekah In the Bible there is the story of God contacting man through Christ but there is also man occupying a very important position The central characters in the Bible are not only God in Christ but also man as the bride of God in Christ The universal couple is God and man In the universe God is the only male and man is the counterpart of God If man is without God he is like a widow If God is without man He is like a bachelor In the universe there has to be the matching of God with man

zh: 所以在旧约起头的地方，头一幕所给我们看见的，就是一个男子需要一个配偶的故事。这一个男子就是预表基督，基督就是神的化身；这一个配偶就是预表教会，教会就是人类中被神所拯救出来，要给神建造的一班人。你再往下看，不要说到新约，就是在旧约的时候，神对祂的百姓就一直是站在一个丈夫的地位上。神一直把以色列人当作祂的配偶。慢慢地主耶稣来了，那位作主耶稣先锋的施浸者约翰不仅喊说，这是神的羔羊，除去世人罪孽的；他也在那里证实说，娶新妇的就是新郎。约翰不仅介绍主耶稣是赎罪的羔羊；也介绍主耶稣是娶新妇的新郎。再到书信里头，使徒保罗说，我把你们这些得救的人，许配给一个丈夫，如同贞洁的童女献给基督。他也说，夏娃之于亚当，正如教会之于基督。到了启示录，就是全圣经末了，有一个宣告说，羔羊婚娶的时候到了。到了新耶路撒冷出来的时候，就说，新耶路撒冷象新妇妆饰整齐，预备好了，等候丈夫。那就是神人合一，所有蒙救赎的人和救赎主成为一个，成了宇宙的奥秘，就是基督与教会。
en: Therefore, at the beginning of the Old Testament, the first scene shown to us is a story of a man needing a counterpart. This man typifies Christ, and Christ is the embodiment of God; this counterpart typifies the church, and the church is a company of people saved by God out of mankind to be built up by God. If you look further, not to mention the New Testament, even in the Old Testament, God always stood in the position of a husband to His people. God always regarded the Israelites as His counterpart. Gradually, the Lord Jesus came. John the Baptist, who was the forerunner of the Lord Jesus, not only cried out, "Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!" but he also testified there, saying, "He who has the bride is the bridegroom." John not only introduced the Lord Jesus as the redeeming Lamb, but he also introduced the Lord Jesus as the bridegroom who takes the bride. Then in the Epistles, the apostle Paul said, "I betrothed you to one husband to present you as a pure virgin to Christ." He also said that Eve is to Adam as the church is to Christ. In Revelation, which is the end of the entire Bible, there is an announcement, saying, "The marriage of the Lamb has come." When the New Jerusalem comes forth, it says that the New Jerusalem is like a bride adorned, prepared for her husband. That is the union of God and man, in which all the redeemed ones and the Redeemer become one, becoming the universal mystery, which is Christ and the church.

zh: 关于圣经的中心，我们还可以换一个说法。基督是神活的道，活的话；圣经是神写的道，写的话。基督是活的话，圣经是写的话。基督是圣经的内容，圣经是基督的说明。把基督从圣经里拿去，圣经变作一本空的书，如同空的器皿没有内容一样；同时没有一个人，不明白圣经而能好好认识基督，因为圣经乃是基督的说明。你只有读圣经这一个说明，才能懂得，才能认识基督是怎样一回事。而圣经所说的，乃是基督的一切摆在教会里，借着教会来彰显。所以圣经的中心乃是基督和教会，光认识基督还不够，还得有教会。圣经里头所给我们看见的，那个宇宙的中心人物，有头，也有身体。头是基督，身体是教会。所以基督和教会乃是圣经的中心。
en: Concerning the center of the Bible, we can also put it another way. Christ is God's living Word, the living word; the Bible is God's written Word, the written word. Christ is the living word, and the Bible is the written word. Christ is the content of the Bible, and the Bible is the explanation of Christ. If Christ is taken out of the Bible, the Bible becomes an empty book, like an empty vessel without content. At the same time, no one can know Christ well without understanding the Bible, because the Bible is the explanation of Christ. Only by reading the Bible, this explanation, can you understand and know what Christ is all about. And what the Bible speaks of is all of Christ being placed in the church to be expressed through the church. Therefore, the center of the Bible is Christ and the church; it is not enough to know only Christ, we must also have the church. The central figure of the universe shown to us in the Bible has a head and also a body. The Head is Christ, and the Body is the church. Therefore, Christ and the church are the center of the Bible.

zh: （一）历史：在五经之后就是历史书。从约书亚记起一直到以斯帖记，共有十二卷：约书亚记、士师记、路得记、撒母耳记上、撒母耳记下、列王纪上、列王纪下、历代志上、历代志下、以斯拉记、尼希米记、以斯帖记。
en: 1) History: After the Pentateuch are the books of history. There are twelve books from Joshua to Esther: Joshua, Judges, Ruth, 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, 1 Kings, 2 Kings, 1 Chronicles, 2 Chronicles, Ezra, Nehemiah, and Esther.

zh: （二）诗歌：都是诗歌体裁，共有六卷：约伯记、诗篇、箴言、传道书、雅歌，这五卷是相联的；还加上耶利米哀歌，它的体裁也是诗歌，不是散文。这六卷在中文看不出来是诗歌体裁，但在原文清清楚楚地是诗歌体裁，是对耦诗歌，是对句的，一点都不是散文的。
en: 2) Psalms: There are six books, all in the style of poems. Five books—Job, Psalms, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, and Song of Songs—are related. Lamentations is also added because it is in the style of poetry rather than prose. In some translated versions, one cannot identify these six books as poems, but in the original, these are clearly in poetic forms, with couplets and matching phrases. They are not at all in the style of prose.

en: 3) The Books of the Prophets: This is the last part of the Old Testament. It can be divided into three categories chronologically.

zh: （1）被掳前的先知书：共有十一卷。若照着写作时间的早晚来排列，最早的一个先知可能是俄巴底亚，第二个是约珥，第三个是约拿，第四个是阿摩司，第五个是何西阿，第六个是以赛亚，第七个是弥迦，第八个是那鸿，第九个是西番雅，第十个是耶利米，第十一个是哈巴谷。耶利米比哈巴谷稍微早一点，但是耶利米却延长到被掳时。他开头作先知，是在被掳前，但在末了的时候，是在被掳时。所以有的解经家把他列为被掳前的先知，有的解经家把他列为被掳时的先知。我们赞成把他列在被掳以前，因为他作先知，大部分的时间是在被掳以前。
en: (1) The Books of the Prophets before Captivity: There are a total of eleven books. If arranged in chronological order according to the time they were written, the earliest one is probably Obadiah, second is daily Joel, third is Jonah, fourth is Amos, fifth is Hosea, sixth is Isaiah, seventh is Micah, eighth is Nahum, ninth is Zephaniah, tenth is Jeremiah, and the eleventh is Habakkuk. Jeremiah was a little earlier than Habakkuk, but Jeremiah was extended into the captivity period. Jeremiah began as a prophet before the captivity and ended as one in the captivity. This is why some Bible expositors consider him as a prophet before the captivity, and others consider him as one during the captivity. We suggest considering him as one before the captivity because he spent most of his time as a prophet before the captivity.

en: (2) The Books of the Prophets during the Captivity: There are a total of two books, which are Daniel and Ezekiel. Daniel and Ezekiel were both prophets during the captivity.

zh: 四卷福音，一卷行传，末了一卷预言，加上二十一卷书信，一共二十七卷。记圣经卷数最好的方法是中文九九乘法表里的三九二十七，旧约三十九卷，新约二十七卷。
en: The four Gospels, Acts, the twenty-one Epistles, plus the last book of prophecy, add up to twenty-seven books. An easy way to memorize the number of books of the Bible is "three times nine equals twenty-seven" in the Chinese multiplication table; that is, there are thirty-nine books in the Old Testament and twenty-seven books in the New Testament.

zh: （二）经历：就是五卷诗歌；约伯记、诗篇、箴言、传道书、雅歌。这五卷虽有一点点历史，但不是讲历史；里头也有一点预言，但也不重在说预言。这五卷乃是重在说到那些活在神面前的圣民，他们在神里面属灵的经历。若是光有前一段的历史，没有后面的经历，我们就只能看到他们所遭遇的史实，却不懂得他们在各样遭遇中，里头的光景是怎样。这五卷诗歌在圣经里，刚刚好就把在神面前的选民，在各种遭遇和经历里，他们里面的光景描述出来。我们读这五卷诗歌，就能知道他们在神面前，那些属灵的经历是怎样。
en: 2) Experience: namely, the five books of poetry—Job, Psalms, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, and Song of Songs. Although these five books contain a little history, they are not about history; they also contain a little prophecy, but they do not emphasize prophecy. These five books rather emphasize the spiritual experiences in God of those saints who lived in the presence of God. If we only had the history of the preceding section without the subsequent experiences, we would only see the historical facts of what they went through, but we would not understand what their inner condition was in their various encounters. These five books of poetry in the Bible exactly describe the inner condition of the chosen people in the presence of God in their various encounters and experiences. When we read these five books of poetry, we can know what their spiritual experiences in the presence of God were.

en: 1) History: The four Gospels plus Acts are five books on history. The four Gospels cover the experiences of the Lord Jesus on earth together with the experiences of His disciples in following Him. Acts shows us how the disciples testified for the Lord everywhere they went. These five books are all on historical facts.

zh: 壹	我们要认识任何一本书，都需要先抓住它的总纲和中心，也需要对它的结构有正确的分析，而清楚认识它的分段；圣经也有它的总纲、中心和分段—提后二15，三16。（李常受文集一九五九年第三册，认识圣经，第三篇）
en: I. If we want to know any book, we have to grasp its subject and central thought. In addition, we need a proper analysis of its structure and a clear understanding of its sections; the Bible has its own subject, its central thought, and its sections.—2 Tim. 2:15; 3:16.

en: A. The Lord Jesus is God's living Word, and the Bible is God's written Word; if the written Word, the Bible, did not have the living Word, the Lord Jesus, as its reality, the Bible would be nothing but empty doctrines and vain letters—2 Tim. 3:16; John 14:6.

zh: 二	有了圣经这清楚确定的说明，明白的启示，主耶稣就能具体的给人认识，确定的给人了解；所以我们若要认识主耶稣，就非读圣经，非明白圣经不可—五39，路二四44。
en: B. Since there is the clear, definite explanation and plain revelation of the Scriptures, the Lord Jesus can be known practically and comprehended definitely by men; hence, if we want to know the Lord Jesus, we must read and understand the Bible—John 5:39; Luke 24:44.

zh: 贰	圣经的功用；在为着我们这一面，圣经的功用第一就是叫我们有得救的智慧，将神在基督里的救法，和人因信得救的途径，启示给我们—提后三15，林前一24。
en: IV. The function of the Bible; on our side, the first function of the Bible is to make us wise unto salvation, revealing to us how God saves men in Christ and how men may be saved by faith—2 Tim. 3:15; 1 Cor. 1:24.
norm_zh: 贰圣经的功用在为着我们这一面圣经的功用第一就是叫我们有得救的智慧将神在基督里的救法和人因信得救的途径启示给我们提后三15林前一24

en: III. The first practical function of the Bible in us is to cause us to be regenerated; the word of the Bible is like a seed of life falling into us, causing us to have God’s life and be regenerated—1 Pet. 1:23; James 1:18.

zh: 肆	圣经使我们得着重生之后，就教训我们，督责我们，使我们在各方面归正，教导我们在凡事上学义，叫我们这蒙了神的重生，得以在神面前成为完全—提后三16~17。
en: IV. After the Bible causes us to be regenerated, it teaches us, convicts us, corrects us in all aspects, and instructs us in righteousness in all things, so that we, who have been regenerated by God, may be complete before God—2 Tim. 3:16-17.

en: V. The teachings of the Bible can also give us endurance, comfort, and hope; when we encounter sufferings, we can easily receive help and establishment from the Bible—Rom. 15:4, 13.

en: VI. Many things are recorded in the Bible as examples for our admonition; when we read these records, we can easily be warned by the experiences of some who went before us, and we can be careful not to follow their example—1 Cor. 10:11.

en: VII. Often the word of the Bible is to us like a lamp shining in a dark place; if we want to be enlightened and knowledgeable, we must understand the Bible and keep the word of the Bible in our hearts so that it can shine and enlighten us at any time—2 Pet. 1:19; Rom. 13:12.

en: VIII. People walking in the dark need a lamp to shine on the path of their feet; if we keep the word of the Bible in our heart, the word of the Bible can become a lamp to our feet and a light to our path—Psa. 119:105; Prov. 6:23.

en: X. In addition to containing the power to enlighten, the word in the Bible has the power to cleanse; enlightenment is in contrast to darkness, and purification is in contrast to filthiness; if we read the Bible frequently, we will not only be enlightened but also kept pure—Psa. 19:9; 119:9.

norm_en: X In addition to containing the power to enlighten the word in the Bible has the power to cleanse enlightenment is in contrast to darkness and purification is in contrast to filthiness if we read the Bible frequently we will not only be enlightened but also kept purePsa 199 1199

en: XI. The Bible also prevents us from sinning against God; if we store the words of the Bible in our heart, they will constantly remind us so that we do not sin against God—v. 11; Job 36:10.

en: XII. The word in the Bible is also the sword of the Spirit, which we can apply by the Holy Spirit to deal with Satan and his messengers; we can defeat the evil spirits, the enemy, who tempt and attack us, all through the word of the Bible—Eph. 6:17-18.

en: XIII. The word of the Bible is as sharp as a sword; not only can it deal with our spiritual enemies, but it can also divide our soul from our spirit and discern the thoughts and intentions of our heart—v. 17; Heb. 4:12.

en: XIV. The Bible is food for our spiritual life; just as our physical life needs nourishment, our spiritual life needs nourishment; the word is the only thing that can supply nourishment to our spiritual life—Jer. 15:16; Matt. 4:4; Job 23:12; Heb. 5:14.

norm_en: XIV The Bible is food for our spiritual life just as our physical life needs nourishment our spiritual life needs nourishment the word is the only thing that can supply nourishment to our spiritual lifeJer 1516 Matt 44 Job 2312 Heb 514

zh: 拾伍	圣经的话不只是我们属灵生命的干粮，也是我们属灵生命的奶；一个初得重生的信徒，必须爱慕圣经的话，“像才生的婴孩爱慕一样”—彼前二2，林前三1~2，来五12~14。
en: XV. The word of the Bible is not only the solid food of our spiritual life but also the milk of our spiritual life; a newly regenerated believer must long for the word of the Bible, "as newborn babes long for it"—1 Pet. 2:2; 1 Cor. 3:1-2; Heb. 5:12-14.

zh: 圣经的第一个功用，是给主耶稣作见证。主耶稣是圣经的题目，是圣经的内容；圣经是主耶稣的说明，是主耶稣的发表。主耶稣是神活的道，圣经是神写的道。圣经这写的道，若没有主耶稣那活的道作实际，圣经就不过是空洞的道理，虚空的字句。主耶稣那活的道，若没有圣经这写的道作发表，主耶稣就是玄妙难得认识，渺茫难得捉摸的。但有了圣经这清楚确定的说明，明白的启示，主耶稣就能具体的给人认识，确定的给人了解。不只新约各书都是启示主耶稣的，就是旧约各部分，无论是1摩西的律法，2先知的书，或是3诗篇，（旧约共分这三大部分，）无不都是为主耶稣作见证，说到主耶稣的。所以我们若要认识主耶稣，就非读圣经，非明白圣经不可。
en: The first function of the Bible is to testify concerning the Lord Jesus. The Lord Jesus is the subject and contents of the Bible; the Bible is the explanation and expression of the Lord Jesus. The Lord Jesus is God’s living Word; the Bible is God’s written Word. The Bible, God’s written Word, must have the Lord Jesus, the living Word, as its reality; otherwise, it is but mere doctrines and empty letters. The Lord Jesus, the living Word, must have the Bible, the written Word, as His expression; otherwise, He is mysterious and difficult to know, vague and hard to grasp. However, since there is the clear, definite explanation and plain revelation of the Scriptures, the Lord Jesus can be known practically and comprehended definitely by men. Not only every book of the New Testament reveals the Lord Jesus, but every part of the Old Testament, whether 1. the Law of Moses, 2. the Prophets, or 3. the Psalms (these are the three major parts of the Old Testament), testifies and speaks concerning the Lord Jesus. Hence, if we want to know the Lord Jesus, we must read and understand the Bible.

zh: 再比方，有一个姊妹正和一个不信的男子进行婚姻。一天她读经读到林后六章十四节，那里所说“你们和不信的原不相配，不要同负一轭”的话，就刺入她的心中，叫她觉出她一个信的人和一个不信的男子进行婚姻，乃是出于她自己的主意，不是出于神的旨意。这样，这节圣经的话，就把她在婚姻的事上，怎样随从她自己的意思，体贴她肉体的爱好，而不随从神的旨意，不体贴神的心意，那真实的光景，给她显明出来；就在她婚姻的事上，把她的心意和神的旨意，分别清楚；就叫她在这样的大事上得蒙拯救，脱离自己肉体的喜爱；不随着肉体和心中行喜好的去行，而顶从神那上好的旨意，使自己蒙到神的喜悦，并得着神的保守。圣经的话在这一类的事上，对于我们常是活泼而有功效的，其锋利甚于两刃的剑。我们里面无论有什么样的调和掺杂，圣经的话都能为我们剖开辨明，而将我们真实的光景带到神约面前，摆在神的面光中，叫我们得蒙拯救，脱离魂，而活在灵里；脱离自己和自己的意念，而活在神和神的心意里。
en: A sister who plans to marry an unbeliever may be touched when she reads 2 Corinthians 6:14, which says, “Do not become dissimilarly yoked with unbelievers.” This word can pierce her heart and cause her to see that her desire to marry an unbeliever is according to her own will, not God’s will. Thus, the word enables her to discern that she is following her will and minding the preferences of her flesh rather than God’s will and heart’s desire in the matter of marriage. When the will in her soul is divided from God’s will in her spirit, she will be saved from the desires of her flesh in this important matter. Rather than following her flesh and the desires of her heart, she will obey the peerless will of God. Then she will please God and be preserved by God. In such matters, the word of the Bible is always living and operative to us, and sharper than any two-edged sword. No matter what kind of mixture we have within us, the word of the Bible can divide and discern it for us, and bring our real condition before God and place it in the light of His face, that we may be saved to deliver us from the soul and live in the spirit, to deliver us from ourselves and our own thoughts and live in God and His heart's desire.

zh: 圣经的话不只是我们属灵生命的干粮，也是我们属灵生命的奶。干粮是为大人的，奶是为婴孩的。当我们在属灵的生命上长大，对于属灵的事能领会得练达的时候，我们就能从圣经的话里，得到干粮的营养，使我们属灵的生命强壮有力。当我们在属灵的生命上幼稚，对于属灵的事，领会力不够强的时候，圣经的话也有的像奶一样，能喂养我们，使我们在属灵的生命上得以渐渐长大。所以一个初得重生的信徒，必须爱慕圣经的话，“像才生的婴孩爱慕一样；”否则，他在属灵的生命上必不能长大，必一直作一个“在基督里为婴孩”的人。
en: The Bible is not only solid food but also milk for our spiritual life. Solid food is for adults; milk is for infants. When our spiritual life is mature and we have an understanding of spiritual matters, we can extract the nourishment of solid food from the Bible, strengthening our spiritual life. When our spiritual life is immature and we lack an adequate understanding of spiritual matters, there are portions of the word of the Bible that are like milk, which can nourish us and cause our spiritual life to grow. Therefore, a newly regenerated believer must love the word of the Bible, “as newborn babes long for it”; otherwise, his spiritual life cannot grow, and he will always be one who is “an infant in Christ.”

zh: 圣经的话，不只能洁净我们外面的行为，去掉我们外面在行为上所受的玷污，并且还能在我们里面洗净我们，叫我们脱离旧造的弱点。以弗所五章这里所说的，就是这种的洗净─就是主要用祂在我们里面生命的水，借着圣经的话，把我们洗净，叫我们脱去旧造的斑点（以弗所五章二十七节的“玷污”，原文是“斑点”）和皱纹。斑点和皱纹，不是我们在外面行为上所受的玷污，乃是我们在里面旧造生命里所有的弱点。这是主要用圣经的话，配合着祂在我们里面的生命，给我们洗去的。圣灵常使圣经的一句或一段话，活现在我们里面，来配合主在我们里面的生命，使我们脱去旧造的东西，而得在新造里长大。这也是圣经的话，在我们里面的一种洗净功用。
en: The word of the Bible washes our outward actions and removes our outward defilement. It also washes us inwardly and frees us from the weaknesses of the old creation. Ephesians 5:26 refers to this kind of washing. The Lord uses the water of life within us to wash us through the word of the Bible, eliminating the spots (the word for “defilement” in Ephesians 5:27 is “spots” in the original text) and wrinkles of the old creation. Spots and wrinkles are not related to the defilement that we acquire from our outward actions but to the weaknesses of the life of the old creation within us. The Lord uses the word in coordination with His life in us to wash away our spots and wrinkles. The Holy Spirit in coordination with the Lord’s life in us frequently enlivens us with a word or sentence in the Bible in order to remove things of the old creation so that we can grow in the new creation. This washing is a function of the word of the Bible.

zh: 陆	圣经中也记载许多的事，作我们的鉴戒，使我们受警戒；我们每逢读到这些记载的时候，很容易得到前车之鉴，而生了戒心，免蹈前辙—林前十11。（李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册，圣经要道（卷三），第三十一题）
en: VI. Many things are recorded in the Bible as examples for our admonition; when we read the Bible, we can be warned by the experiences of some who went before us, and we can be careful not to follow their example—1 Cor. 10:11.
norm_zh: 陆圣经中也记载许多的事作我们的鉴戒使我们受警戒我们每逢读到这些记载的时候很容易得到前车之鉴而生了戒心免蹈前辙林前十11李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册圣经要道卷三第三十一提
norm_en: VI Many things are recorded in the Bible as examples for our admonition when we read the Bible we can be warned by the experiences of some who went before us and we can be careful not to follow their example1 Cor 1011

zh: 柒	圣经的话对于我们，许多时候也像明灯照在暗处；我们若要作一个明亮、通达时务的人，就必须明白圣经，有圣经的话存在心中，随时发光照亮我们—彼后一19，罗十三12。（李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册，圣经要道（卷三），第三十一题）
en: VII. Often the word of the Bible is to us like a lamp shining in a dark place; if we want to be enlightened and knowledgeable, we must understand the Bible and keep the word of the Bible in our hearts so that it can shine and enlighten us at any time—2 Pet. 1:19; Rom. 13:12.
norm_zh: 柒圣经的话对于我们许多时候也像明灯照在暗处我们若要作一个明亮通达时务的人就必须明白圣经有圣经的话存在心中随时发光照亮我们彼后一19罗十三12李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册圣经要道卷三第三十一提
norm_en: VII Often the word of the Bible is to us like a lamp shining in a dark place if we want to be enlightened and knowledgeable we must understand the Bible and keep the word of the Bible in our hearts so that it can shine and enlighten us at any time2 Pet 119 Rom 1312

zh: 捌	人在黑暗里走路，是需要灯光照亮脚步的；把圣经的话存记在心，圣经的话就能作我们脚前的灯，路上的光—诗一一九105，箴六23。（李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册，圣经要道（卷三），第三十一题）
en: VIII. People walking in the dark need a lamp to shine on the path of their feet; if we keep the word of the Bible in our heart, the word of the Bible can be a lamp to our feet and a light to our path—Psa. 119:105; Prov. 6:23.
norm_zh: 捌人在黑暗里走路是需要灯光照亮脚步的把圣经的话存记在心圣经的话就能作我们脚前的灯路上的光诗一一九105箴六23李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册圣经要道卷三第三十一提
norm_en: VIII People walking in the dark need a lamp to shine on the path of their feet if we keep the word of the Bible in our heart the word of the Bible can be a lamp to our feet and a light to our pathPsa 119105 Prov 623

zh: 玖	圣经的话所发出的光，不只能在我们所行的路上照亮我们的脚步，还能叫我们愚昧人变为通达—诗一〇九103，弗五17。（李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册，圣经要道（卷三），第三十一题）
en: IX. The light emitted by the word of the Bible not only can enlighten our steps on the path we walk, but can also cause us foolish people to become understanding—Psa. 109:103, Eph. 5:17.

norm_en: IX The light emitted by the word of the Bible not only can enlighten our steps on the path we walk but can also cause us foolish people to become understandingPsa 109103 Eph 517

zh: 拾	圣经的话不只有照亮的能力，也有洁净的能力；照亮是对黑暗的，洁净是对污秽的；我们若常读圣经，不只必蒙光照，也必蒙洁净—诗十九9，一一九9。（李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册，圣经要道（卷三），第三十一题）
en: X. In addition to containing the power to enlighten, the word in the Bible has the power to cleanse; enlightenment is in contrast to darkness, and purification is in contrast to filthiness; if we read the Bible frequently, we will not only be enlightened but also kept pure.—Psa. 19:9; 119:9.
norm_zh: 拾圣经的话不只有照亮的能力也有洁净的能力照亮是对黑暗的洁净是对污秽的我们若常读圣经不只必蒙光照也必蒙洁净诗十九9一一九9李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册圣经要道卷三第三十一提
norm_en: X In addition to containing the power to enlighten the word in the Bible has the power to cleanse enlightenment is in contrast to darkness and purification is in contrast to filthiness if we read the Bible frequently we will not only be enlightened but also kept purePsa 199 1199

zh: 拾壹	圣经也能使我们免得犯罪得罪神；我们若将圣经的话藏在心里，圣经的话就能常常提醒我们，使我们免得犯罪得罪神—11节，伯三六10。（李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册，圣经要道（卷三），第三十一题）
en: XI. The Bible also prevents us from sinning against God; if we store the words of the Bible in our heart, they will constantly remind us so that we do not sin against God.—v. 11; Job 36:10.
norm_zh: 拾壹圣经也能使我们免得犯罪得罪神我们若将圣经的话藏在心里圣经的话就能常常提醒我们使我们免得犯罪得罪神11节伯三六10李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册圣经要道卷三第三十一提
norm_en: XI The Bible also prevents us from sinning against God if we store the words of the Bible in our heart they will constantly remind us so that we do not sin against Godv 11 Job 3610

zh: 拾贰	圣经的话也是圣灵的宝剑，是我们可以靠着圣灵用以对付撒但和他的使者的；我们能打败那引诱或攻击我们的邪灵、仇敌，都是藉着圣经的话—弗六17~18。（李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册，圣经要道（卷三），第三十一题）
en: XII. The word in the Bible is also the sword of the Spirit, which we can apply by the Holy Spirit to deal with Satan and his messengers; through the word of the Bible, we can defeat the devil, the enemy, who tempts and attacks us.—Eph. 6:17-18.
norm_zh: 拾贰圣经的话也是圣灵的宝剑是我们可以靠着圣灵用以对付撒但和他的使者的我们能打败哪引诱或攻击我们的邪灵仇敌都是借着圣经的话弗六1718李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册圣经要道卷三第三十一提
norm_en: XII The word in the Bible is also the sword of the Spirit which we can apply by the Holy Spirit to deal with Satan and his messengers through the word of the Bible we can defeat the devil the enemy who tempts and attacks usEph 61718

zh: 拾叁	圣经的话锋利如剑，不只能对付我们属灵的仇敌，并且能将我们里面的魂与灵给我们剖开，能将我们心中的思念和主意给我们辨明—17节，来四12。（李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册，圣经要道（卷三），第三十一题）
en: XIII. The word of the Bible is as sharp as a sword; not only can it deal with our spiritual enemies, but it can also divide our soul from our spirit and discern the thoughts and intentions of our heart.—v. 17; Heb. 4:12.
norm_zh: 拾叁圣经的话锋利如剑不只能对付我们属灵的仇敌并且能将我们里面的魂与灵给我们剖开能将我们心中的思念和主意给我们辨明17节来四12李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册圣经要道卷三第三十一提
norm_en: XIII The word of the Bible is as sharp as a sword not only can it deal with our spiritual enemies but it can also divide our soul from our spirit and discern the thoughts and intentions of our heartv 17 Heb 412

zh: 拾肆	圣经的话也是我们属灵生命的食物；我们肉身的生命如何需要营养，我们属灵的生命也如何需要营养；属灵生命的营养，是只有圣经的话能供应的—耶十五16，太四4，伯二十三12，来五14。（李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册，圣经要道（卷三），第三十一题）
en: XIV. The word of the Bible is also food for our spiritual life; just as our physical life needs nourishment, our spiritual life needs nourishment; the word is the only thing that can supply nourishment to our spiritual life.—Jer. 15:16; Matt. 4:4; Job 23:12; Heb. 5:14.
norm_zh: 拾肆圣经的话也是我们属灵生命的食物我们肉身的生命如何需要营养我们属灵的生命也如何需要营养属灵生命的营养是只有圣经的话能供应的耶十五16太四4伯二十三12来五14李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册圣经要道卷三第三十一提
norm_en: XIV The word of the Bible is also food for our spiritual life just as our physical life needs nourishment our spiritual life needs nourishment the word is the only thing that can supply nourishment to our spiritual lifeJer 1516 Matt 44 Job 2312 Heb 514

zh: 拾伍	圣经的话不只是我们属灵生命的干粮，也是我们属灵生命的奶；一个初得重生的信徒，必须爱慕圣经的话，“像才生的婴孩爱慕一样”—彼前二2，林前三1~2，来五12~14。（李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册，圣经要道（卷三），第三十一题）
en: XV. The word of the Bible is not only the solid food of our spiritual life but also the milk of our spiritual life; a newly regenerated believer must long for the word of the Bible, “as newborn babes long”.—1 Pet. 2:2; 1 Cor. 3:1-2; Heb. 5:12-14.
norm_zh: 拾伍圣经的话不只是我们属灵生命的干粮也是我们属灵生命的奶一个初得重生的信徒必须爱慕圣经的话像才生的婴孩爱慕一样彼前二2林前三12来五1214李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册圣经要道卷三第三十一提
norm_en: XV The word of the Bible is not only the solid food of our spiritual life but also the milk of our spiritual life a newly regenerated believer must long for the word of the Bible as newborn babes long1 Pet 22 1 Cor 312 Heb 51214

zh: 拾陆	圣经的话，不只能洁净我们外面的行为；并且还能在我们里面洗净我们，叫我们脱离旧造的弱点；叫我们脱去旧造的斑点—弗五16~17，约十五3。（李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册，圣经要道（卷三），第三十一题）
en: XVI. The word of the Bible not only can wash our outward actions; it also can wash us inwardly, freeing us from the weaknesses of the old creation and eliminating the spots of the old creation.—Eph. 5:16-17; John 15:3.
norm_zh: 拾陆圣经的话不只能洁净我们外面的行为并且还能在我们里面洗净我们叫我们脱离旧造的弱点叫我们脱去旧造的斑点弗五1617约十五3李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册圣经要道卷三第三十一提
norm_en: XVI The word of the Bible not only can wash our outward actions it also can wash us inwardly freeing us from the weaknesses of the old creation and eliminating the spots of the old creationEph 51617 John 153

zh: 拾柒	圣经的话也非常有能力，能像火焚烧，并能像大锤打碎；圣经的话能把人向着神冰冷的心烧得火热，也能把人与神圣洁不合的东西烧灭净尽—耶二三29，五14。（李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册，圣经要道（卷三），第三十一题）
en: XVII. The word of the Bible is also very powerful; it is like a burning fire and a smashing hammer; the word of the Bible can burn hearts that are ice cold toward God and can completely burn away the things of man, which are contrary to God’s holy nature.—Jer. 23:29; 5:14.

norm_en: XVII The word of the Bible is also very powerful it is like a burning fire and a smashing hammer the word of the Bible can burn hearts that are ice cold toward God and can completely burn away the things of man which are contrary to Gods holy natureJer 2329 514

zh: 拾捌	圣经的话也像雨、露、甘霖，能灌溉、滋润；我们是神所耕种的田地，是神所栽种的庄稼；圣经的话使我们生长结实—林前三9，可四20，林前三6。（李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册，圣经要道（卷三），第三十一题）
en: XVIII. The word of the Bible is also like rain, dew, and abundant showers; it waters and refreshes us; we are God's farm, the harvest that God cultivates; the word of the Bible causes us to grow and bear fruit.—1 Cor. 3:9; Mark 4:20; 1 Cor. 3:6.
norm_zh: 拾捌圣经的话也像雨露甘霖能灌溉滋润我们是神所耕种的田地是神所栽种的庄稼圣经的话使我们生长结实林前三9可四20林前三6李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册圣经要道卷三第三十一提
norm_en: XVIII The word of the Bible is also like rain dew and abundant showers it waters and refreshes us we are Gods farm the harvest that God cultivates the word of the Bible causes us to grow and bear fruit1 Cor 39 Mark 420 1 Cor 36

zh: 拾玖	圣经的话不只像雨，也像雪滋润我们；雨是在春、夏、秋三季有的，雪是在冬季有的；无论在什么时候，圣经的话都能滋润我们—赛五五10~11。（李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册，圣经要道（卷三），第三十一题）
en: XIX. The word of the Bible is not only like rain, but it also refreshes like snow; rain comes in the spring, summer, and fall, but snow comes in the winter; the word of the Bible can refresh us in every season of our condition—Isa. 55:10-11.
norm_zh: 拾玖圣经的话不只像雨也像雪滋润我们雨是在春夏秋三季有的雪是在冬季有的无论在什么时候圣经的话都能滋润我们赛五五1011李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册圣经要道卷三第三十一提
norm_en: XIX The word of the Bible is not only like rain but it also refreshes like snow rain comes in the spring summer and fall but snow comes in the winter the word of the Bible can refresh us in every season of our conditionIsa 551011

zh: 贰拾	圣经的话也像面镜，能照出我们的本像，映出我们的真情；许多人都是因着读圣经，而看见了自己的真面目，认识了自己的真光景—雅一23，林后三18。（李常受文集一九三二至一九四九年第三册，圣经要道（卷三），第三十一题）
en: XX. The word of the Bible is also like a mirror; it reflects our true appearance and condition; by reading the Bible, we see our real countenance and know our true condition—James 1:23; 2 Cor. 3:18.

norm_en: XX The word of the Bible is also like a mirror it reflects our true appearance and condition by reading the Bible we see our real countenance and know our true conditionJames 123 2 Cor 318

en: XXI. The Bible can restore and refresh our soul, make us wise, make our heart joyous, and enlighten our eyes—Psa. 19:7-8.

en: XXII. The Lord’s words—the word of the Bible—are spirit and life; therefore, the word of the Bible enables us to have the Spirit and life; it causes us to receive life from the Spirit and to live by the Spirit—John 6:63; Rom. 8:4.

zh: 然而有的人就要说，现在的信条，是可从圣经里，用许多的证据，证明都是圣经自己的教训的。好，如果圣经会教训信条所教训的，圣经是像信条那样的有权威，则何必在圣经之外，又有信条呢？人或若要以为：我们知道圣经的教训，真是专一的，满足的；然而，圣经若真有专一的教训，又何必你们出来用信条叫它成为专一的呢？如果圣经是有权威的，则何必用信条来证明圣经的权威呢？信条的权威，足以证明圣经的权威么？这样的作法，乃是羞辱圣经，并非尊重圣经！圣经自己的见证是说，“圣经都是神所默示的，于教训、督责、使人归正、教导人学义，都是有益的；叫属神的人得以完全，预备行各样的善事。”（提后三16~17）。
en: However, some say that the present creeds can be proved to be the very teaching of the Bible by many scriptural proofs. Very well. If the Bible teaches what the creeds teach, and if the Bible is as authoritative as the creeds are, why then do we need the creeds in addition to the Bible? Some have conceded that the teachings of the Bible are specific and complete. If the teaching of the Bible is, indeed, so specific, why then is there the need to make it more specific with the creeds? If the Bible is indeed so authoritative, why then is there the need to prove its authority with the creeds? Can the authority of the creeds prove the authority of the Bible? To do this is to put the Bible to shame. It is not to honor the Bible! The Bible testifies of itself: "All Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for conviction, for correction, for instruction in righteousness, that the man of God may be complete, fully equipped for every good work" (2 Tim. 3:16-17).

zh: 人以信条所记载的，是有权威的，就是取消圣经的权威！叫人不以圣经为程度，而以信条为程度！如果不幸，在信条里有了错误；则人们也应当维持这个错误，像维持其中其他的真理一般。如果不幸，在信条中有了缺点，则圣经也没有机会，可以补满它；简言之，这样的作法，就是取消圣经的高位，叫人的良心不能直接在神面前负责。所以，现在敬畏神的人们，应当起来，反对一切人所用以代替神的话的规则。
en: For man to consider the creeds as authoritative is for him to annul the authority of the Bible! It causes man to take the creeds as the standard instead of taking the Bible as the standard! If unfortunately there are faults in the creeds, man must uphold these faults in the same way that he upholds all the truths, and if there are shortages in the creeds, the Bible will have no opportunity to make up these shortages. Simply put, this way annuls the high place given to the Bible and bars man's conscience from being directly responsible to God. Hence, all God-fearing men should now rise up to oppose all ordinances used by man to replace God's word.

zh: 无论如何，耶洗别好像是很有智慧的。她以为她自己是可以教导人的，她就连接着管理人。她的错处，就是她不肯让她假冒为神话语的教训，给神的话语来审判，看到底是真是假。她也知道，神所默示的，是有权威的；所以她才假冒她是受神默示的。然而，她忘记了，她这样的受神默示，是否神所默示的话语所允许的。她的权威，不许人疑问，只许人接受。圣经也是如此。它是绝对应当被人接受的。就是为着这个缘故，所以它在过去的时代中，曾受过许多的试验。人的试验越厉害，圣经的权威越显明。真的并不怕人试验。并且一受试验，反将假的显明出来！相信罗马的，乃是愚昧与迷信。相信圣经的，乃是聪明，并满有理由。（倪柝声文集第一辑第五册，基督徒报（卷三），默想启示录（中卷），（四）推雅推喇（罗马的教会））
en: Jezebel may seem very wise. She thinks that she herself can teach others. As a result, she becomes dominating over others as well. Her problem lies in the fact that she is not willing to have her counterfeit teachings to be judged by the Word of God itself and to test if her teachings are indeed true or false. She knows that God's inspiration is authoritative. That is why she counterfeits God's inspiration. However, she forgets whether the way she thinks she is inspired is itself something that is warranted by the inspiration of God. She can entertain no questioning of her authority; one must accept it fully. The same is demanded by the Bible; it requires absolute acceptance. It is for this reason that during the past ages there have been numerous tests. The more man tested it, the more obviously the authority of the Bible manifested itself. All true things can withstand tests. Tests will only expose the false things! It is foolishness and superstition to believe in anything Romish. On the contrary, it is wise and very reasonable to believe in the Bible.(CWWN, vol. 5, "The Christian (3)," SUB-SECTION FOUR  THYATIRA-THE ROMAN CATHOLIC CHURCH (2:18-29)

zh: 我是一个全心相信圣经的人。照我看来，圣经是最高的法庭，凡圣经所定规的，我们毫无权利可以稍加疑议。圣灵知道教会应当如何组织，祂已经在圣经里完全启示出来了；乃教会中人竟有以为圣经中所启示的教会组织法，是尚属幼稚的，处今世界进化（？！）的光景中，应当有更完善的组织─究竟这不过是照着罗马教会的原路而进，究竟这不过是自大自高的世人，表明他们轻看神的心意而已。现今中国教会正处过渡的时代，多人都是题本色的教会；但是，本色而不合经，究非主旨；空洞洞的以“中华基督教会”为名，究有何益。愿主在这背道的世代中叫我们忠心！（教会的组织法，请读本报第四期全册）（倪柝声文集第一辑第七册，基督徒报（卷五），问答（四））
en: I, for one, believe the Bible with my whole heart. To me, the Bible is the highest court. Whatever is shown in the Bible, we do not have the slightest right to doubt, even a little. The Holy Spirit knows how the church should be organized. He has revealed the matter completely in the Scriptures. However, some in the church feel that the church organization revealed in the Bible is immature and that there should be a better and more complete organization in this age of progression. Actually, this is to follow the same road that the Roman Catholic Church has taken. These are but haughty people who despise the will of God. Today, the churches in China are in a transitional period. Many talk about indigenous churches, but to be indigenous without being scriptural is not the will of the Lord. zh: 摩西的五卷书（摩西五经）：在神圣启示的进展里，有神圣启示的进步。在创世记，有神与祂的创造。在出埃及记，有神的救恩与祂居所的建造。在利未记，有蒙救赎者的敬拜与生活。在民数记，我们看见神所救赎的人编组成为神的军队，以及他们为神争战的行程。申命记重申神圣的律法，不仅是摩西五经的结语，也是律法的结语。（民数记生命读经，第一篇；申命记生命读经，第一篇）
en: The five books of Moses (the Pentateuch): In the progress of the divine revelation, there is an advancement of the divine revelation. In Genesis there is God and His creation. In Exodus there is God's salvation and the building of His dwelling place. In Leviticus there is the worship and living of the redeemed. In Numbers we see God's redeemed people formed into God's army and their journeying to fight for God. Deuteronomy rehearses the divine law, being the conclusion not only of the Pentateuch but also of the law.
norm_zh: 摩西的五卷书摩西五经在神圣启示的进展里有神圣启示的进步在创世记有神与祂的创造在出埃及记有神的救恩与祂居所的建造在利未记有蒙救赎者的敬拜与生活在民数记我们看见神所救赎的人编组成为神的军队以及他们为神争战的行程申命记重申神圣的律法不仅是摩西五经的结语也是律法的结语民数记生命读经第一篇申命记生命读经第一篇
norm_en: The five books of Moses the Pentateuch In the progress of the divine revelation there is an advancement of the divine revelation In Genesis there is God and His creation In Exodus there is Gods salvation and the building of His dwelling place In Leviticus there is the worship and living of the redeemed In Numbers we see Gods redeemed people formed into Gods army and their journeying to fight for God Deuteronomy rehearses the divine law being the conclusion not only of the Pentateuch but also of the law

zh: 历史书—约书亚记、士师记、路得记、撒母耳记上和下、列王纪上和下、历代志上和下、以斯拉记、尼希米记与以斯帖记

norm_en: The books of historyJoshua Judges Ruth 1 Samuel 2 Samuel 1 Kings 2 Kings 1 Chronicles 2 Chronicles Ezra Nehemiah and Esther

zh: 照着从约书亚记到以斯帖记所记载的历史，其内在的启示乃是向我们揭示，神永远的经纶如何在地上由祂的选民所施行。首先，约书亚记给我们看见，如何取得、占有、并守住美地。然后，士师记、路得记、撒母耳记上、下这几卷书，描绘出一些人的图画，给我们看见他们在得了美地为业之后，如何留在美地上，并如何享受美地。在士师记里所记载的几位士师，路得记里所记载的路得和波阿斯，撒母耳记上、下所记载的以利、撒母耳、扫罗、约拿单、大卫，呈现一幅幅生动的图画，给我们看见这些人如何留在美地上，并如何享受美地。虽然那些图画刻画得很详细，但仍然需要列王纪上、下提供更多人物的图画，给我们看见他们如何留在美地上，并如何享受美地。以斯拉记与归回耶路撒冷重建圣殿有关；尼希米记与修复、重建圣城有关；以斯帖记给我们看见，无所不在、无所不能的神，如何成了隐藏的神，保护在被掳中祂分散的选民。
en: According to the history recorded from Joshua to Esther, its intrinsic revelation is to unveil to us how God's eternal economy is carried out on earth by His elect. First, Joshua shows us how to take, possess, and keep the good land. Then the books of Judges, Ruth, and 1 and 2 Samuel depict pictures of certain persons to show us how, after they inherited the good land as an inheritance, they stayed in the good land and enjoyed the good land. The judges recorded in Judges, Ruth and Boaz in Ruth, and Eli, Samuel, Saul, Jonathan, and David in 1 and 2 Samuel present vivid pictures showing us how these persons stayed in the good land and enjoyed the good land. Although those pictures are depicted in detail, 1 and 2 Kings are still needed to provide more pictures of various persons to show us how they stayed in the good land and enjoyed the good land. Ezra is related to the return to Jerusalem to rebuild the temple; Nehemiah is related to the recovering and rebuilding of the holy city; and Esther shows us how the omnipresent and omnipotent God became a hidden God to protect His scattered elect in captivity.

en: The Minor Prophets focus on four main points: God's loving chastisement of Israel and His governmental dealing with Israel, His judgment upon the nations, the manifestation of Christ, and the restoration of all things. Although the Minor Prophets are smaller, the revelation brought in by these books is great. The central point of the divine revelation in the Minor Prophets is the same as that in the Major Prophets.
